name: full-plunge
description: Serve a ball, hold s_plunger past plungerMaxHoldTicks (full strength), release, and reach the main field. Also carries the DW-66 observable (ball_launched + ballsInPlay becoming 1).

friction.source: authored: midpoint of addendum §2's 'Flipper friction' range 0.8-0.9 (AR-17) -- "what makes centre shots and backhands possible"; no artifact states a single value

scatter.source: addendum §2 physics tuning table, 'Scatter angle': "0, for every era; randomness is tuned down"

mass.source: lib/vpt/flipper/flipper-data.ts @ e8a6d6f: FlipperData.updatePhysicsSettings()'s registry.getRegStringAsFloat('Player', 'FlipperPhysicsMass${idx}', 1) fallback default -- the vpx-js 'modern era' override value, transcribed since DragonWar has no per-table override-physics system of its own (AD-1) and this IS the modern band physics-tuning.md's 'Flipper strength' note says to inherit

strength.source: lib/vpt/flipper/flipper-data.ts @ e8a6d6f: FlipperPhysicsStrength${idx} fallback default 2200 (VPX internal solenoid-strength unit, dimensionless) -- the modern-era band

rampUp.source: physics-tuning.md:28 "Coil ramp-up 2.5 -- Solenoid acceleration time -- enables the light tap. Source: VPE default via the brief addendum §4" (supersedes flipper-data.ts's own FlipperPhysicsCoilRampUp fallback of 3.0 for this table)

torqueDampingAngleDeg.source: lib/vpt/flipper/flipper-data.ts @ e8a6d6f: FlipperPhysicsEOSTorqueAngle${idx} fallback default, degrees

sweepDeg.source: lib/vpt/flipper/flipper-data.ts @ e8a6d6f: FlipperData field defaults startAngle 121.0 / endAngle 70.0 -> the ported ROTATION MAGNITUDE |121-70| = 51; the committed collision geometry supplies the flipper's absolute table-frame pose (see loader/index.ts and this story's Design Notes, "How the bat is derived from the committed box")

endRadiusRatio.source: lib/vpt/flipper/flipper-data.ts @ e8a6d6f: FlipperData field defaults endRadius 13.0 / baseRadius 21.5 -- the ported dimensionless taper ratio; the committed collision geometry supplies the absolute base radius (half the bat's own width)

rollover.source: AD-2 rule text: "defaults by class: rollover 0, standup target 8, drop target 20, bumper skirt 2, tilt bob 0"

button.source: authored: AD-2 states button switches (s_start, s_flipper_l, s_flipper_r, s_plunger) are emitted by sim/loop from InputFrame transitions, never through physics debounce, so there is no bounce to settle

slam.source: authored: AD-5 states the slam detector's closure is a tick-windowed nudge-count threshold computed in physics, not a debounced analog switch

defaultPitchDeg.source: FR-10 consequence text; AD-10 TABLE.reference.pitchDeg; addendum §2 reference geometry ("pitch 6.5°... high confidence")

pitchMaxDeg.source: FR-10 consequence text: "range 6.0-8.5° [ASSUMPTION: bounds]"; corroborated by addendum §2 "competition range 6.5-8.5°"

hopControl.source: authored: FR-9 states the two-endpoint behaviour (0 = no hops, default = occasional hops on hard hits) but no unit or magnitude; hop.ts (this story) supplies both -- measured this pass against the paired hopControl=0-vs-default stress replay (test/hop-control.test.ts) to produce a clear, glass-safe margin without every hard hit turning into a launch

slamNudgeWindowMs.source: authored: FR-16 states the mechanism but no window duration

tiltWarningSpacingMs.source: authored: AD-3 names "tilt spacing" as a rules timer; FR-14 states the debounce requirement, no duration

tiltSettleMs.source: authored: AD-3/AD-7 name "tilt... settle" as a rules timer keyed to the bob's physical decay; no duration stated

plungerMinHoldMs.source: authored: AD-5 states the mapping exists ("plungerSpeedByHoldMs"), not its curve; a bare tap is the ramp's lower bound

plungerMaxHoldMs.source: authored: AD-5 states the mapping exists, not its curve; the ramp's upper bound before the plunge is full power

plungerMinSpeedScale.source: authored: fraction of full plunger power at plungerMinHoldMs

plungerMaxSpeedScale.source: authored: fraction of full plunger power at plungerMaxHoldMs and beyond

troughEjectSpeedMmPerS.source: authored: AD-6 requires an eject speed, no artifact states one -- measured against the real loop (not just a standalone physics probe) to stay inside sw_shooter_lane's own y <= 60 mm zone ceiling for its whole arc (peak y ~50.6 mm), avoiding the spurious ball_launched a higher speed (500 mm/s, peak y ~105.6 mm) produces by overshooting the zone before settling

autolaunchSpeedMmPerS.source: authored: AD-6 requires an eject speed, no artifact states one -- measured during Story 1.5 planning against col_lane_deflector, whose clearance threshold sits between 1600 and 1800 mm/s; this carries margin above it

massKg.source: vpinball/vpinball @ 3f838c14b: src/physics/cabinet/CabinetPhysics.h:24, CabinetPhysics(float mass = 113.f) default ctor argument

nudgePeakAccelG.source: vpinball/vpinball @ 3f838c14b: src/physics/cabinet/KeyboardNudge.cpp:162-164, comment "0.5g max peak accel on strong nudge" (baseScale = 0.5f * g / coreScriptStrength, with coreScriptStrength = 2.f the reference "full strength" nudge)

flipperTipGapMm.source: authored: derived arithmetic, not a second invented figure -- the gap between the right bat's tip (col_flipper_r.bboxMm.min.x = 277.525 mm) and the left bat's tip (col_flipper_l.bboxMm.max.x = 236.875 mm) at end-of-stroke, both a direct consequence of DW-78's reconciliation (each box moved outward by baseRadius = 12.5 mm around its own unchanged pivot). No planning artifact states a tip gap the sourced 9.5-12.7 mm figure (digests/geometry-r1-1.md:91,204, low confidence) is narrower than the 26.99 mm reference ball and therefore unusable as authored truth (Code Map, "Read-only evidence")

outlaneWidthLeftMm.source: authored: no sourced figure carries a left/right split -- the closest artifact is geometry-r2-1.md:16,78's 1-3/8 in = 34.9 mm inlane/outlane width (low confidence, no side named), adopted here as the LEFT outlane's clear width, measured from col_wall_left's interior face (table x = 0) to col_guide_divider_l's outlane-facing face (tools/make-placeholder-blend.py)

outlaneWidthRightMm.source: authored: the same geometry-r2-1.md low-confidence 1-3/8 in = 34.9 mm figure as outlaneWidthLeftMm, adopted symmetrically for the RIGHT outlane -- but measured from col_wall_lane's main-field face (table x = LANE_X0_MM = 468.4 mm), not the true right perimeter wall, because the plunger lane already claims the space between col_wall_lane and that wall (tools/make-placeholder-blend.py, add_drain_triangle_side())

ringBounceDamping.source: vpinball/vpinball @ 3f838c14b: src/physics/cabinet/PlumbHandler.cpp:118, m_plumbOmega *= 0.8f; // magic damping factor

dampingScale.source: authored: upstream reads this from Settings::GetPlayer_PlumbDamping(), a user setting with no value in any of the seven authorized vpinball/vpinball files -- 1.0 (identity) is the most defensible 'no adjustment' choice against the transcribed dampingCoef0/dampingCoef1 ratio coefficients; measured during this story's implementation (see spec Verification section) to leave a single ordinary nudge's peak swing (~1.05 deg) well clear of thresholdDeg while still permitting a rapid nudge burst to cross it and decay away within a few seconds. Story 1.9's feel ritual ratifies it

thresholdDeg.source: authored: upstream reads this from Settings::GetPlayer_PlumbThresholdAngle(), a user setting with no value in any of the seven authorized vpinball/vpinball files -- measured during this story's implementation (see spec Verification section) so that ONE ordinary nudge_* rising edge (peak swing ~1.05 deg, measured) never crosses it, while a rapid burst of nudges (a deliberate, violent 'slam'-style burst) does. Story 1.9's feel ritual ratifies it against the Reference machine

notes: stateHash() hashes the whole game tree, which includes machine.deviceSlots -- this golden therefore freezes the LOOP-WRITTEN value of deviceSlots (sim/loop/index.ts:341-344, the live AD-7 violation tracked as DW-70) as part of its reference hash. If Story 2.5's fix is faithful the values will be identical and nothing breaks; if this golden ever breaks on deviceSlots alone, check DW-70 before assuming the physics changed. Story 2.1b (2026-09-01): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed against the completed shot-map registry and collision document (TABLE gains ~31 switches, 7 coils and bd_lock; the collision document gains ~27 col_ nodes), header.gameStart.tuning unchanged (no TUNING value moved). expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash moved: bd_lock adds a slots entry to every snapshot's machine.deviceSlots, changing GameState's own shape regardless of trajectory -- booted [true, true, true] under the then-unconditional fill(true) default, corrected to [false, false, false] by Story 2.1d (see that story's own note below); 'empty-slots' was never accurate for this pass. Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01), correcting this note: the sentence that used to stand here -- blaming "Blender's alphabetical bpy.data.objects ordering" reshuffling existing nodes' own array positions, with an "order-sensitive broadphase" -- was investigated and found FALSE, twice: the collision document is alphabetically sorted throughout, so the ~28 new names interleave among the existing ones rather than reshuffling their relative order, and a document rebuilt with the rework's own wall-height and deflector changes reverted reproduces the two affected goldens bit-identically, ruling out node reordering as the mechanism. The TRUE cause of the two affected goldens' own trajectory divergence was not identified by either the implement pass or this rework; DW-53's wall-height change (col_wall_left/_top/_right/_lane now reaching the glass) and DW-58's col_lane_deflector removal were both tested and ruled out individually (each reproduces the divergence bit-identically when reverted alone). State plainly rather than guess further: the trajectory changed because the shot map's own regeneration changed the collision document in some way this investigation did not isolate -- not because of the specific mechanism previously claimed here. This golden's own recorded scenario was re-verified against the refreshed run and still holds at the recorded transitions/coilPrologue/durationTicks (byte-identical, untouched). Rework iteration 3 (2026-09-02): header.assetHash refreshed again (the deflector re-site / col_loop_top shorten / sw_drain widen, DW-121). expectedHash moves too -- this golden's own 2000-tick window genuinely reaches the re-sited deflector and the shortened col_loop_top (final ball position this pass: x = 79.7, y = 1025.8, past both), so its own exact quantised position shifts; expectedGameStateHash is UNCHANGED (30f802cb), confirming no switch/device state differs, only the ball's own continuous position. The covering assertions (ball_launched once, ballsInPlay = 1, ball.pos.x < LANE_X0_MM) still hold. Story 2.1c (2026-09-03), the ORBIT: header.assetHash refreshed and the trajectory RE-RECORDED. The GameState-only hash is UNCHANGED (30f802cb before and after) -- only the ball's own path moved, not the game state -- which is the expected shape for a geometry change that does not alter what the rules see. Traced before recording: the plunged ball still clears the Loop entrance, still crosses the top of the table (max y 1053.2 mm, against this story's own > 1040 mm criterion) and still ends on the main field (final x 40.7 mm, well inside the < 468.4 mm the scenario below asserts), riding the re-joined col_loop_top toward the Left Loop's lane rather than dropping off its shortened end into open field. Code review pass 2 rework (2026-09-03): header.assetHash refreshed (a DRAGON-bank/leg-width re-solve elsewhere on the table, and a col_loop_top north-face ridge fix -- 2.5 mm, symmetric about the connector's own midpoint -- closing a genuine DW-119-class stranding this rework's own new test discovered: a ball released at rest anywhere on col_loop_top's own PREVIOUSLY FLAT north face made zero positional progress). This golden's own path rides that exact face, so it is the one most directly touched by the second fix. Re-verified before recording: AC 4's own standing test (max y tracked across the whole run, > 1040 mm) still passes, and this golden's own scenario check (ball_launched once, ballsInPlay 1, final x < 468.4) still passes. expectedHash moved (d53a20f9 -> 6f4d54d3); expectedGameStateHash did NOT (30f802cb unchanged) -- the game-relevant state is byte-identical, only the exact quantised ball position at the final tick shifted (the ridge's own 2.5 mm drop is well inside this margin for a ball crossing at >= 1100 mm/s, per that fix's own note in tools/make-placeholder-blend.py). Story 2.1d (2026-09-03): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed again -- bd_lock now declares startsFullAtBoot (dragonwar.ts) and boots [false, false, false] rather than the previous (wrongly unconditional) [true, true, true], the Lock lane's three slot zones moved into the corridor col_dragon_leg_l/_r already bound, the eject/one-ball-per-pulse fix landed, and col_spinner_l was renamed vis_spinner_l (a presentation mesh, absent from the collision document). Traced: this golden's own plunge trajectory never approaches x [150, 190] (the Lock lane's own x-span) at any point -- it climbs the shooter lane and crosses the top of the table, per its own AC 4 checkpoint (max y > 1040 mm) -- so none of this pass's geometry changes touch its path. expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash moved for exactly one reason: every snapshot's own machine.deviceSlots.bd_lock changes from [true, true, true] to [false, false, false], which is exactly AD-6's own 'the machine carries 4 balls, asserted at boot' behaviour this story's AC 1 requires. Re-verified against the real runReplay() pipeline: DW-70's own two wrapper literals ([true,true,true,true] / [true,true,true,false]) are unaffected (bd_trough alone), and this golden's own AC 4 checkpoints (ball_launched once, ballsInPlay 1, max y > 1040 mm) still hold.
